ownership.insiderDesc: No founding family in control: Reed Hastings (co-founder, Executive Chairman) remains the largest individual shareholder (~21,16M shares post-split) but directors and officers as a group represent only a minority fraction of the capital, with no share class carrying enhanced voting rights. Notable governance event: Hastings will NOT stand again for the board at the 2026 annual meeting.

items.title: Securities class action alleging that Netflix concealed from investors the slowdown in its subscriber growth (including the impact of password sharing) between January 2021 and April 2022.
items.allegedBy: Shareholder plaintiffs (including Grant & Eisenhofer, Kirby McInerney, Rosen Law Firm), federal court in California
items.outcome: Final dismissal by the federal judge in November 2024, the court holding that a further amendment of the complaint would be futile - case closed.
items.source: Law360, StreamTV Insider (couverture du rejet, novembre 2024).

items.title: Investigation solicitations by several plaintiff law firms (including Robbins Geller Rudman & Dowd, Schall Law Firm) into possible misleading statements by Netflix and its executives regarding the group's business and operations.

compliance.note: A former class action (2022, subscriber growth/password sharing) was definitively dismissed in November 2024. A wave of investigation solicitations by plaintiff firms has existed since late October 2025 (see items) but remains at the most preliminary stage - no precise subject of allegation and no formal complaint identified to date, no regulatory investigation (SEC/DOJ) recorded.

clesRetenues: Q Sean Diffley (Morgan Stanley) - lessons from the Warner Bros. Discovery situation and appetite for M&A: Neumann/management describe the deal as 'nice-to-have, not need-to-have', team stayed focused on the core business, capital discipline demonstrated by walking away when the cost exceeded the value for shareholders.
Q Vikram Kesavabhotla (Baird) - performance of the internal engagement-quality metric in 2026: new all-time high in Q1, credibility assessed through its predictive power on retention.

Q Rich Greenfield (LightShed) - impact of the Nielsen methodology on advertising revenue: Nielsen Gauge is not the currency of the video market, a change with no effect on effectiveness, 3 Md$ advertising target maintained.

Q John Hodulik (UBS) - viewership details for the World Baseball Classic and similar opportunities: 31,4M viewers, most-watched programme in Japan's history, biggest sign-up day in the country's history, strong associated APAC growth.

Q Robert Fishman (MoffettNathanson) - assessment of the ROI of live events vs scripted content, NFL strategy: strategy unchanged (big landmark events), NFL discussions ongoing within a disciplined, event-centred framework.

Q Peter Supino (Wolfe Research) - business model and strategy for podcasts: early data showing incremental engagement, notably during the daytime and on mobile, promising owned and licensed catalogue.

Q Dan Salmon (New Street Research) - growth of the advertiser base, direct buying vs DSP, mid-market strategy: advertiser base +70% year on year to more than 4 000, programmatic approaching 50% of non-live ads, iterative expansion.

Q Vikram Kesavabhotla (Baird) - rationale and early signals from the US price increase: pricing based on value improvements and engagement signals, early results in line with expectations and with history, stronger retention everywhere.

Q Eric Sheridan (Goldman Sachs) - lessons from 5 years of video games and future investment focus: 150 Md$ addressable market identified, synergistic IP extensions, platform games supporting retention/acquisition, kids' games prioritised.
Q Brian Pitts (BMO) - how the success of Netflix Playground is measured and its value for the subscriber: dedicated kids' games app, curated, with no ads or in-app purchases, strong growth signals.
Q Eric Sheridan (Goldman Sachs) - competitive landscape by geography/format: strong creator relationships beyond budget alone, recent signings with top-tier talent as an indicator of repeat business.

Q Eric Sheridan (Goldman Sachs) - evolution of the GenAI creative process and rationale for the InterPositive acquisition: GenAI improves the tools, not the art; InterPositive accelerates a filmmaker-specific technology, growing adoption among creators.

Q Rich Greenfield (LightShed) - timing of Reed Hastings' exit from the board and its link to Warner Bros. Discovery: exit unrelated to the WBD situation (which Reed had himself championed), transition reflecting a succession philosophy long announced by the founder.

Q Steve Cahall (Wells Fargo) - driver of the FX-neutral growth deceleration Q2->Q3: Neumann answers that it is not steered quarter by quarter, identical drivers (subscriptions/price/advertising), some choppiness tied to a 2025 base more weighted to H2, annual target of 13-14% maintained, penetration <45% of addressable households and only ~7% of the 670 Md$ addressable market captured.

Q Rob Sanderson (Loop Capital) - engagement quality despite the slowdown in view hours per member: Peters answers that the hours/revenue relationship is not linear (e.g. live = 5% of the content budget but 1% of hours, yet 6 of the 10 best sign-up days over 5 years), viewing hours +2% in H1 26 (acceleration vs +1,5% in 2025).

Q Steve Cahall (Wells Fargo) - acceleration of content amortisation vs value for the member: Sarandos answers that content spend is growing ~10% in 2026 (vs an 8% average over 5 years, 14% over 10 years), disciplined investment, strong slate (I Will Find You, Swapped, Teach You a Lesson, The Polygamist).

Q David Joyce (Seaport) - concern about the audience drop for season 2 releases: Sarandos answers that there is no material change in aggregate, the season 2 drop-off is slightly improved vs last year, no change to release strategy planned.

Q Vikram Kesavabhotla (Baird) - retention/engagement follow-up after the World Baseball Classic in Japan: Sarandos confirms a record success (most-watched programme in Japan's history), live events generate sign-up spikes with slightly higher churn but in line with expectations, continued expansion of the live calendar including regional events.

Q Robert Fishman (MoffettNathanson) + Rich Greenfield (LightShed) - bundling opportunity (Peacock, FAST channel) and TF1 as a third-party platform: Peters answers that it is too early (4 weeks) but the results are encouraging, openness to similar partnerships, nothing new to announce.

Q Robert Fishman (MoffettNathanson) - opportunity for a free FAST offering: Peters answers that the option is being studied but with no near-term launch plan, cannibalisation risk and the need for an advertising business already at scale.

Q John Hodulik (UBS) - future content formats beyond games/podcasts: Sarandos declines to pre-announce, says he is encouraged by podcasts (incremental daytime/mobile viewing), new publisher partnerships (Conde Nast, Hearst, People) the following month.

Q Steve Cahall (Wells Fargo) - advertising monetisation potential (ARM): Peters answers that the ARM gap between the ad tier and the standard tier is narrowing and represents an under-realised revenue opportunity, driven by the broadening of demand sources and the proprietary ad-tech stack.

Q Sean Diffley (Morgan Stanley) - receptivity to price increases and timing/magnitude: Peters answers that the H1 26 increases (US, Mexico, Spain) are going as planned, price always follows value already delivered, Netflix remains the best value in the SVOD sector.
Q Rich Greenfield (LightShed) - return of free trials in certain markets: Peters confirms free-trial tests for new, non-resubscribing members (outside the US/UK), a standard test-and-learn approach.

Q Vikram Kesavabhotla (Baird) - progress on the cloud gaming strategy: Peters cites a 150 Md$ addressable market (excluding China/Russia), FIFA and Unhinged as the best cloud launches, cloud monthly active players x11 since October 2025, kids' games (Playground) mobile engagement +600% year on year.

Q Jessica Reif Ehrlich (BofA) - leverage from scale (~330M households) in a consolidating media landscape: Sarandos answers that scale creates a flywheel effect (discovery, monetisation, programme ROI), TF1 as an example, sector consolidation is nothing new, focus remains on members.

Q Sean Diffley (Morgan Stanley) - early lessons from the InterPositive acquisition and its impact on the 20 Md$ content budget: Sarandos answers that GenAI is being extended to around 300 titles (concentrated in post-production), quality preserved (artists in control), savings probably reinvested in more content rather than cut from the budget.

Q Dan Kurnos (StoneX) - capital allocation in the face of the Lionsgate/NBCUniversal rumours: Sarandos declines to comment on the speculation, reaffirms the 'builders not buyers' philosophy and a very high bar for any significant M&A; Neumann confirms no change to capital allocation policy, record buyback of 4,7 Md$ in Q2, 27 Md$ of authorisation remaining.

dernierCall.guidanceProchainTrimestre: Q3 26 guided: revenue ~$12.86B, +12% reported / +11% FX-neutral - slightly below the pre-print consensus (~$13.0B, ~13% growth); operating margin 33.2%, net income $3,452M, EPS $0.82. Management frames the optical FX-neutral deceleration (12% -> 11%) as comp-driven (2025 revenue was more back-half weighted), with unchanged drivers: membership growth, pricing, and scaling ads revenue.
dernierCall.guidanceAnnuelle: FY26 revenue tightened to $51.0-51.4B (13-14% reported, ~12% FX-neutral, ~$6B incremental YoY) around the unchanged $51.2B midpoint; operating margin reiterated at 31.5%; advertising revenue on track to roughly double to ~$3B (vs ~$1.5B in 2025); cash content spend ~$20B, content expense +10% YoY - deliberately below revenue growth (vs 8% 5-yr and 14% 10-yr averages). Management: halfway through the year, tracking to the 2026 financial plan. Normalized FY26 consensus EPS (S&P Global, ex one-offs) $3.51.
pointsCles: Record $4.7B share buyback in the quarter (largest in company history, partly funded by the WBD break-up fee), ~$27B authorization remaining; capital-allocation philosophy unchanged and 'builders, not buyers' reiterated against Lionsgate/NBCUniversal speculation - a very high bar for any large M&A.

Engagement narrative defended in depth: view hours +2% in H1 26 (vs +1.5% in 2025), no linear hours-to-revenue link (live = 5% of content budget but ~1% of hours yet 6 of the top-10 signup days in 5 years); Season 2 falloff slightly improved YoY, so no change to the all-at-once release strategy.

Monetization levers on track: H1 price increases (US, Mexico, Spain) performing in line with history, ad-tier ARM gap vs the standard plan narrowing on the proprietary ad stack ('near-term underrealized revenue'), free-trial tests for new members in select markets, and the TF1 (France) integration encouraging four weeks in - no FAST or free tier planned near term.

GenAI now used on ~300 titles (mostly post-production; InterPositive, Eyeline, animation lab) - the 'American Experiment' docuseries shipped 17 minutes of AI-enhanced footage twice as fast at half the cost, with savings to be reinvested into content; FY26 content spend +10%, still below revenue growth; cloud-gaming MAUs up 11x since Oct-25 and kids mobile-game engagement +600% YoY.

hypothese.summary: Global streaming leader, revenue growth guided at 13-14% for 2026 and operating margin expansion confirmed (31,5% guided). WBD termination fee of 2,8 Md$ (Q1 26) excluded from omniumNet as non-operating. Record buybacks in Q2 26.
hypothese.text:
== THESIS SUMMARY ==
Undisputed streaming leader (~1bn viewers) with under 45% penetration of an ~800M-broadband-household TAM where it captures only ~7% of ~670bn addressable revenue. The compounding stack: subscription growth + pricing power + advertising ramp (~3bn targeted 2026 vs ~1.5bn 2025), with content-cost growth guided ~10% - below revenue growth - feeding steady margin expansion (operating margin 31.5% guided). FY26 revenue tightened to 51.0-51.4bn at Q2.

== THESIS READ ==
- The ad tier is the marginal thesis driver: 2x targeted in 2026 and still early. Watch: ad-revenue milestones vs the ~3bn goal.
- Margin expansion is policy, not luck (content growth capped below revenue growth). Watch: content-slate inflation and sports-rights discipline.
- Capital returns accelerate: shares -2.4%/yr modeled, gross-debt cap 10-15bn maintained. Watch: buyback pace vs the WBD situation (any large M&A would break the model).

== SPECIAL FACTORS ==
Base = normalized operating (ex-WBD-related items per ancrages). Normative tax 14% (2025 actual 13.7%, no windfall to correct). Historical net debt 2015-2021 approximated (low confidence flagged, moderate materiality). Post-split share figures.

== PARAMETERS & WATCH-LIST ==
Revenue +12%/yr fading to +9% by 2030; EBIT margin 31.5% -> 34%; ETR 14%; finNet ~-500M shrinking with modest deleveraging (5.5 -> 3bn). Published 2025 reconciles at ~0 residual. Shares 4,200 -> 3,800M. Watch: FX-neutral vs reported growth gap; ad-tech stack execution; engagement metrics disclosure cadence.

== CATALYSTS ==
Q3 (Oct); ad-revenue disclosures; 2027 guidance (Jan); live/sports events scaling.

ancrages.moteur: 2026 revenue guided at 51,0-51,4 Md$ (13-14% reported, ~12% FX-neutral), slowing gradually towards ~9% in 2030 as the base dilutes, supported by household penetration <45% and a captured addressable market share of only around 7%.

2026 operating margin guided at 31,5% (vs 29,5% in 2025), with content costs (+10% guided) growing more slowly than revenue; gradual expansion continuing towards ~34% by 2030 as operating leverage materialises.

Gross termination fee of 2,8 Md$ received in Q1 2026 following the abandonment of the Warner Bros. Discovery acquisition (Paramount Skydance counterbid), booked in "interest and other income" — excluded from 2026 omniumNet/omniumEPS as a non-operating and non-recurring gain, consistent with the treatment of non-operating gains elsewhere in the portfolio.
Tax rate normalised at 14%, close to the 2025 effective rate (13,7%) with no sign of a windfall to correct, applied stably across the whole projection horizon.

Record buyback in Q2 26 (4,7 Md$, partly funded by the WBD termination fee), ~27 Md$ of authorisation remaining; diluted shares assumed to decline continuously from ~4,3 Md (2025) towards ~3,8 Md by 2030.

Gross debt ceiling targeted by management at 10-15 Md$ (no further deleveraging committed), but the growing free cash-flow (9,5 Md$ in 2025) is assumed to reduce net debt gradually despite the pace of buybacks.

2025.residualNote: Reconciles cleanly: ~600M net interest on the gross-debt stack (10-15bn cap policy), actual 2025 ETR 13.7%.

annualBeatHistory.note: Initial FY25 guidance (Q4-24 letter, 21/01/2025): revenue 43.5-44.5bn (mid 44.0) and 29% operating margin - implied op income 12.76bn; realized 45.0bn at 29.5% = 13.28bn - level +4.0% on the guided op-income plan (revenue alone +2.3%).

Initial FY24 guidance (Q4-23 letter, 23/01/2024): 24% operating margin - Netflix guided no FY24 revenue range, so the beat is margin-only: realized 26.7% = +11.3% on the guided profitability plan (an outsized beat year: margin raised three times in-year).
